html:
Who He Is

Neymir, nicknamed the Werewolf, is a Shavan, a horseman from the ganta of Cort and one of the best scouts of the Moran horde. (Ganta Kort) He had previously served as a mercenary in Shimmery, Darkwater, Milllands, Hope and Sunset Coast and had gone everywhere for his own. He himself said that he knew all the lands in the world, except for Origin and Northwood. He knew the manners of all lands on the right bank of the Holliwell and could speak as a local in any land except the north. Hence the nickname. For three years he served in the Shimmer Orcad and knew it so well that he could describe the view from the windows of the nursery in the merchant's mansion on the Port Pass. He rubbed with the spearmen of the Lion Rocks, the knights of the jungle, the wind-horses of Holliwell, the Northwood "bears" and even with kairs. According to his story, in the army of the Count of the Sunset Coast, he defeated the Kirov officer and slept for two years on the cloak removed from him. In Shimmery, he fought in the War of Velmozh, when the Third and Fourth of the Five attacked the Second. He saw all the styles of fencing of the West, South and Center and owned five perfectly - a rarity for the Steppe, which gives birth to many riders and shooters, but few blade masters.

Neymir is literate, knowledgeable in the legends and customs of different lands. He was careful, sensible and eloquent; he was the one who went to negotiate when it was necessary to make peace with someone, and Chara then grumbled and called him a rag. He hated the regular army for its low salary and eternal expectation, but he knew its order: in any army, not the commander, but the main storekeeper knows everything about everything. Chara laughed at his dream of a quiet old age: “The house is warmer than a tent, and the bed is softer than the earth.” For five years, he traveled with the Scar Without Fear, which was his beloved; both were called “Satellite”. (Chara)

"A Doll on the Throne"

Raid with ganta Birai

In January 1775, after the failure at Melorange, Neymir and Chara went on a foraging raid on the deserted villages of Litland in the gauntdom of Biray, from which thirteen horsemen remained after the battle. (Ganta Birai) Neymir tried to argue with the cruel and short-sighted ganta, but silently: "there was no point in arguing." Birai put the Sputniks on patrol in the forest above the farm, and when the Lithuanian knights came to the village, he threw them and ran away. Neymir whistled the gaunt path to the forest, hoping that he would bypass the enemy, but Biray did not return. The companions defeated the knights themselves: Chara beat with a bow, and Neymir, having entered the detachment, put two and killed a horse under the third. When the two of them returned to the horde, Birai deserted with the remains of the ghana.

Court's Order

In the winter of 1774–1775, after the defeat at Melorange, Neymir saw famine and executions decomposing the horde. Passing by deserters pinned to poles, he wanted to finish off the living with arrows out of pity - "this is what wolves do, not people" - but Chara kept him. When Ganta Kort, to whom the Companions owed their lives, began to cautiously extort their opinion of Moran, Neymir sensed the wrong and replied with an evasive steppe proverb: "The river flows..." “The horse is riding,” Chara picked up.

Court told them to pay their debt and kill Moran. Neymir objected that he paid his debts in battles, not by jackal deeds, and that the rider respected the leader, but not a slave to him. He insisted on talking to Moran first: if the chief had a sensible plan, there was no reason to kill him. In Moran’s tent, he directly demanded to explain why intelligence is needed, otherwise “you will need another intelligence officer.” Moran laughed and revealed to them the plan to burn the Shimmery fleet and go to Shimmery. Neymir felt relieved and then made fun of Chara, who admitted that he was right.

Neu Luccum of Orcada

Moran sent Sputniks as scouts to Melorange. On the way, in the abandoned Melville, the Companions obtained southern clothing from three marauders; Neymir spoke over the dead "Tyria ton of tirya" - they were looters, but still warriors. In Melorange, he entered under the guise of the Shimmer merchant Nei Lukkum of Orcad, and Charu gave up for the purchased altessa. It was from the guard at the gate that the Companions learned of the death of the Lord Adrian; Neymir immediately realized that this would make it more difficult for Moran to hold the horde. After buying up the silver of Major Cly-Colon’s Captenarmus with a bitter taste, he learned that the fleet would dock in the Livny Forest on January 20, and that only two companies were guarding the harbor. Seeing the surveillance, he did not allow Chara to kill the spies and ordered him to spend the night in a hotel, as a merchant should, so as not to alert the enemy. In the morning they were drunk and seized in a stable. Neymir could fight back with a dagger, but then Charu would be stabbed, and he surrendered, playing a frightened merchant.

During his interrogation, he played the merchant so convincingly — he named his father Kalim-Lukkum, Oberlik's mentor, his three ships, their shipyards, and the fact that tea, not silk, was traded in Orcade — that Prince Hector almost believed. (Hector of Shimmery) Hector's maiden, who accused him of lying, he "estimated" only one hundred and ten ephesas, instead of the five hundred that the prince paid - pointing out her shortcomings and inability to remain silent when not asked. However, Hector had a letter of “one gang” with the names of the scouts. Neymir tore his arm out of his belt and tried to strangle the prince, and when he ordered Chare's legs to be cut off, he betrayed Moran's plan. Before his execution, he persuaded the guard to release his legs to die "like a horseman", tore down the cross to which he was tied, and fought, carrying it on his back. From the execution of the Companions saved the sorcerer, demanding in return to bring him to Moran. (Mik)

Exposing Moran

On the way from Melorange, Neymir deduced that the horde had left the old camp too long ago and not towards the Rain Forest. Returning to the horde, which, meanwhile, had defeated Hector, the Companions first decided that they had been betrayed by the gauntlet of Court, and almost killed him, but Neymir, "listening to the heart," believed his excuses. Then he tied it all together: Moran told him to find a "birdhouse" (a dove) in advance, and the horde left through the jungle even before the Satellites were captured. So Moran himself turned his scouts in to lure Hector out of town. Neymir threw this accusation in the face of the chief, beat his blow and cut his thigh to the bone, and Chara crushed Moran's knee. The companions had to flee from the Steppe. “It couldn’t have been otherwise,” Neymir said.

With the Magician and the Newcomer

On the way to Hope, Neymir entertained Chara with legends - about the tears of the golden eagle and about the goddess of sleep, who had gone to the shepherd for seventy years. In the inn they met the Sorcerer again: he was angry that the Companions, recommending him to Moran, themselves mutilated the leader, but hired them, along with the men of the Gant Biray, to rob the banks of the Earl of Shayland in the free cities of Almer and Hope; (Duchy of Almera) Neymir traded a share of four riders for the pair. In March 1775, a gang robbed banks in the free cities of Almera. The sorcerer ordered everyone to be killed, and the Companions stood by while the men of Birai slaughtered the servants; each day they grew increasingly gloomy and hardly spoke to each other. When Shavan Haggott was seriously injured in the fourth bank, Neymir pointed to the lights of the village where a doctor could be found; (Haggot) The sorcerer left him with him, and Charu let him see if the wounded man was alive. When Sorcerer tried to intimidate Chara for the service of mercy, Neymir formulated his credo:

“The wolves of the Origins are killed for pleasure, the dogs of the emperor are killed at his command, wild animals are killed for food, and people kill only when it is impossible to do without it. We are people.”

A “newbie” joined the squad. When questioned by Birai, Neymir determined that he grew up in a castle, studied in a boarding house and, most likely, an outcast who violated the knightly code. Angered that the Newcomer had left Charu alone in the city, Neymir grabbed him on blades. The novice turned out to be a master of the imperial capital school; Neymir changed his style three times, eventually knocked the opponent down with a kick and fist and put a sword to him - but he noticed that he had waited twice, not wanting to kill him, and recognized an honest man in him: "Words can lie, the blade can not." He warned Novichok that Chara is a free woman, but if he offends her, no style of combat will help him. In Laxette, the raid on the bank turned into a trap: signal gongs struck, and the city gate closed. At the gate, Neymir took a blow on his sword, intended for Shavan Gurlach, and in confusion looked for Charu with his eyes, until she took the crossbowman's arrow from the loophole. The newcomer led the detachment out of the city, and then deprived the sorcerer of power, removing the belt-Object from him, and announced that he was catching sorcerers. Neymir and Chara decided that he was really a master, and they followed him to the Hunt.

At the end of March, at the cemetery near Laxett, the Hunter buried the Witch in the burial well, leaving him a bamboo breathing tube, and he gave out where to look for the owner of the Rings: "Tower-Tooth, Bottomless Failure, Second of the Five." Waiting for recognition, Neymir told the Hunter that he and Chara were riders of the Ganta of Cort and walked with Moran "for the free of the West", that the leader had betrayed them and that they had crippled both his legs - let all his life quiver, "like a creep". Sending the rest, the Hunter left the fate of the Witcher in the hands of the Companions: the world will become cleaner if you leave him to die, but their debt will be repaid if you save.

The “Yanmei Hunt”

In May 1775, a detachment of the Hunter - the Ganta of Birai with people, Neymir and Chara - captured the balloon of Harmon Paula, and the Hunter presented his companions to the captive. Neymir disliked the Hunter: Chara looked at him with adoration. He was the only one who openly contradicted the commander; when the prisoner Harmon confessed, Neymir offered to finish him off, and when the Hunter took Charu into the basket of the balloon, not him, he was outraged: “We are Chara — Satellites, we are scouts!”

In the Abode of the Abyss, he shared with Harmon an insult to the "spoiled lord", who seems that there is no law for him, and promised that he would "pay". He asked Harmon to leave with him and pick up his shavanka, and then rushed to the colonel of the Golden Swords mercenary regiment with an order that the prisoner of the Second of the Five wrote under duress. The regiment did not leave, and the prisoner of the Second of the Five (Count Quindar) stated that Neymir betrayed their plan. Chara did not believe it, but later told Alanis that her companion, out of jealousy, led the enemy to the castle, which she defended, and then disappeared without a trace. The betrayal of Neymir is not shown, but everything points to him. The hunter was Lord Adrian.

In "Fantasies"

Return

The author calls the stories “Fantasies” possible destinies of heroes. Closer to Further begins with the great horde splitting up in Fliesse in August 1775: the northern part led by the Gaunt Gaunt was defeated under the walls of the First Winter, and the southern part led by Johan Reis and the Ganta Corta plundered Almera and the Crownlands. After the death of Gnoi-Ganta and Juhan Reis, Kort declared himself the ruler of the Steppe. In "Closer - Further" Neymir, who had long been considered dead, came to Rei-Roy on the May day of 1776, at the head of a group of southern mercenaries, and puzzled the ganta Cort, who became the leader of the Steppe, about a commodity "that can be touched, but cannot be taken." The answer was himself. Kort would forgive him only if Neymir could negotiate with the North, and sent him as ambassador to Erwin Origin, telling him to look at Minerva at the same time. Five comrades from the St. Straus Brigade and two archers of Cort went with Neymir; on the way both offered him their bed and were refused. Court wanted to send his horsemen with him to look after the ambassador, but none of the men ventured into the wolf's den; only the women volunteered. The path lay through Reis and Milllands, past Arina, Milana and Jenna and the silent Rust Giants. In Fairis, the ambassadors chartered a small vessel and circled Polaris from the northwest, replenishing supplies in the Barony of Davey and the Gran Islands. In the Belomorye, they offered their condolences to the recently widowed Lady Fleming, reported to the captain of the Virginia garrison and, under the supervision of the kairs, drove to the First Winter. Everywhere Neymir pretended to be a merchant from Orcada, and the deception was not revealed anywhere. He called only the vassal of the duke, and he called him a brave man.

Ambassadors arrived in the First Winter in the summer of 1776, right on the twentieth birthday of Minerva, when a holiday was buzzing in the castle. Together with the ambassadors of Fairis and the Sunset Coast, a “southern noble named Neu Luccum” appeared with congratulations, and Minerva found such “ignorance” annoying: official delegations accepted on a special day. Erwin, who purposely arranged their arrival for the holiday, spoke with the ambassadors in his office while the guests danced in the courtyard.

Negotiations with Erwin

Erwin, who met him in the office with the question that Stepi’s son would tell him “before he was hanged,” Neymir told about his grief: his beloved served Adrian and died, and he lost himself for a whole year with wine and women, fell into prison for beating a usurer, fled, joined the “warriors of St. Strauss” and the month of silenced the yearnings. He said that he had not fought in either the northern or southern horde and did not believe that the Ganta Pus existed at all. He offered Erwin the votes of Stepi in the election of the lord: in the House she has four votes, two from Reis and two from Holliwell. On behalf of Cort, he offered a tribute of a thousand horses, three thousand cows, and two Sacred Subjects. Erwin replied that in the North honor is more expensive than money, and promised for a tribute of only three years not to fight with Reis.

Erwin demanded a “terrible legend” that would teach the Steppe to appreciate peace with the North. He rejected the tales of the Duke's duel with the Gnogo-Ganta and the Agatha the Radiant. The third legend of Neymir — about the Spirit of the Worm, who created two demons, the god of the Underworld and the Ganta Pus, to split Polaris — Erwin praised, but felt that she lacked fear. Then he proposed his own, cruel: Ambassador Stepi allegedly strangled one of the two archers on the orders of the Duke of Wolves. Neymir rejected it in the morning: the Steppe is so frightened by the winter retreat, when two out of ten survived, and the legend should give cause for pride. He composed another - Pus-ganta, disillusioned with the weak Shavans, he left them and went to other worlds, after which the kairs overcame the horde. Erwin admitted that this legend is better than his own. The Duke then took the ambassadors to the glacier under the castle, where the ice-frozen Count Benedict Fleming and the bodies of the murdered Shavan leaders were kept, and put the condition of friendship: the body of the Shavan that almost killed Erwin would be taken to Rei-Roy, and whenever the northern ambassadors visited, the Chief Stepey would have to kiss his icy face.

Peace and the ashes of Chara

Along with the fellow rayon girls, Neymir on his knees begged for forgiveness from Minerva, who was called by the Shavans "a maiden flying through the sky." Minerva, who received the ambassadors only the next evening, demanded in exchange to give her one of the khanid vir kanna. Then Neymir, who called himself "the first horseman of the Ganta of Cort", signed a preliminary peace agreement with Erwin on behalf of the ten largest Gantts of the Steppe. Minerva his mobile, full of life experience face remotely resembled Inji Price. This scene was followed through the Bird by a one-armed Shavan Zlataya Griva, who served Adrian. (Golden Mane) He believed that Neymir and the archers kissed the feet of the impostor, "like frightened whores", and volunteered to kill them for the lord.

Finally, he asked Erwin “as a warrior warrior” to show the grave of Chara. Erwin took him to the basement, where a signed clay vessel with her ashes was stored; Neymir pressed the vessel to his chest and whispered silently over it, and Erwin, himself almost sobbing, allowed Chara to be taken to the Steppe.

Personality

Neymir is the most “civilized” of the Shavans of the cycle: a cunning man, an actor, and a diplomat. At the same time, he firmly adheres to the steppe concepts of freedom and honor: the rider respects the leader, but not his slave; a person kills only by necessity. For Chara's sake, he was willing to sacrifice everything, even the plan of the entire horde, and jealousy eventually destroyed their union.

Relationships

Chara

Chara was his companion, lover and partner in battle: he fell, she shot. He often read her thoughts without words and knew when she needed to be angry. For her, he gave Hector Moran's plan, and then reproached himself: "Because of me, everyone will die." Chara's feeling for the Hunter aroused jealousy in him, which apparently pushed him to betrayal. He mourned her death for a year.

Moran

Neymir had long defended Moran before Chara as a good general who had won three battles out of four, and was initially happy with his plan. Upon learning that the chief had cold-bloodedly sacrificed the Companions, he mutilated him himself.

The Hunter (Adrian)

The duel with Novichok ended in mutual respect, but later Neymir hated the "spoiled lord", believing that he imagined himself above the law.

Trivia

  • Ganta Court called the Sputniks “hard-boiled rams” who would never become gants — after they nearly killed him by mistake.
  • In Fantasia, Neymir speaks to Court with a "strong southern accent", suggesting that he be sent to the wolves not by Ambassador Stepi, but by "Ney Luccum, a sailor and wanderer from the white-stone Orcad".
  • In the St. Straus brigade, according to Neymir, he dreamed of "an iron ostrich gliding from the sky Star".

Appearances

  • "A Doll on the Throne" - the first appearance ("Satellite - 1"); POV chapters "Satellite" (together with Chara).
  • The Yangmei Hunt is in the chapters of Harmon (Hunter's Squad).
  • "Humans and Gods" is mentioned in the story of Chara Alanis.
  • "Fantasies" is the story "Closer - Further".
